gates.reason: Reads only fixed repository paths derived from import.meta.url, performs no writes, and executes no commands or network requests.
Isolation-contract test only; it does not parse measured artifacts, calculate recommendations, or emit validated fix snippets.
One-shot source/manifest contract test, not production hot-path or shipped runtime code.
The agent-facing doc_neighborhood tool accepts an unrestricted filesystem root and returns content-derived results to the MCP client, permitting prohibited ~/.claude egress.
Recommendation payloads are passed through unchanged; top-friction selection is delegated, and doc-neighborhood output preserves structured hygiene provenance and stale-status demotion.
HTTP tools make one request per invocation, while the bounded local producer has a 20-second timeout and 8 MiB output limit; no N× request-path recomputation was found.
Preview startup uses a fixed executable and argument array without a shell, binds to loopback, and constructs browser URLs from numeric port input rather than executable text.
The benchmark silently trusts any process already occupying the requested port, then labels its results as the intended SPA and 18-session corpus without verifying either.
This is the dedicated render-churn probe; browser contexts isolate runs, long-task totals are summed directly, and three-run medians are calculated from numerically sorted samples.

findings.title: Unrestricted doc root can send ~/.claude-derived content to the subscription LLM
findings.what: Caller-controlled root is forwarded to the host-side document walker and used as its working directory. The resulting document paths, headings-derived graph data, hygiene details, and provenance are serialized into the MCP response consumed by Claude. Nothing rejects ~/.claude or confines traversal to an approved workspace, violating ADR 0008's no-~/.claude-content egress boundary.
findings.fix: Canonicalize the requested root before spawning, reject ~/.claude and descendants, and restrict roots to explicitly approved workspace directories; return an MCP error before invoking the producer when validation fails.
findings.acceptance: With a temporary HOME containing ~/.claude/docs/secret.md whose heading includes a sentinel, invoke doc_neighborhood with root set to that ~/.claude directory and assert the call is rejected and the sentinel is absent from stdout and the MCP response; also verify an approved workspace root still succeeds.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the root is accepted by the public tool schema, copied unchanged into argv and cwd, and producer stdout is returned verbatim as MCP text. The directly related baseline producer resolves that root and reads root Markdown plus docs/**/*.md, so the egress path is concrete.

findings.title: Benchmark can report unrelated occupied-port content as authoritative SPA measurements
findings.what: When the port is occupied, startPreview assumes the intended server is running without checking its identity, build, or corpus. Playwright then measures whatever responds and the report unconditionally claims an isolated SPA measurement over an 18-session sample corpus. An unrelated static server can therefore yield plausible zero-long-task results mislabeled as the target benchmark.
findings.fix: Fail closed on an occupied port unless an application-specific readiness endpoint and corpus/build identity assertion match the expected fixture; print corpus/build provenance from the verified response rather than a hard-coded claim.
findings.acceptance: Start an unrelated HTTP server on the requested port and assert the script exits nonzero before launching measurements; start the intended preview with the expected fixture and assert the report includes verified build and corpus identifiers.
findings.verifyNote: The adversarial second pass re-read the occupied-port branch, navigation target, and report headers. There is no intervening identity, content, build, or corpus check before measurements and the unconditional 18-session claim.
